acceptance: Text-only inline HTML (kbd, ins, samp, strike, tt, var) stays editable marks with its tags hidden, also inside a task item; an image alone in its block and a centered picture render as HTML blocks; a blocked root, an incomplete or mismatched run and an anchor with an unsafe link stay visible source.

An HTML block keeps its safe content while unsafe parts are reduced: an unknown tag, a marquee and a form wrapper are reduced to their text, script and style payloads and event handlers are removed, a table loses its column group but keeps its cells, an ordered list keeps a valid start (an invalid one falls back to 1), a pixel image width applies while an expression or a percentage is left out, and the block survives its reductions (the product's reduction diagnostics are inspection data, not shown); native audio and video are user-controlled players that never autoplay.

reason: Natively HTML renders only as its own block. Inline HTML runs stay visible source: images, linked images and theme pictures inside a paragraph, list item, task, heading, quote or table cell (README badge and download-card lines), passive elements such as font, big, dfn, nobr, meter or an inline center, Markdown inside an inline run, an HTML block on the same line as a list or quote marker, empty elements that the product hides, and inline audio. With no runs there is also no run reveal on caret entry, fold on caret exit, selection spanning a run, nested blocked element reduction inside a run or isolated table-cell run preview.

The native HTML surface applies block alignment, ordered list starts and pixel image sizes, but not percentage image widths, image placement (align left/right), table alignment and width, cell width and vertical alignment or ordered list types, so their valid and invalid values are not distinguished either; and a picture always shows its fallback image, never a candidate chosen by its source's media condition (no dark-mode picture).

TS puts inline SVG into the live DOM, so it must remove scripts, foreign content, animation, linked uses, event handlers and remote paint or style references and prefix local ids. The native surface rasterizes a drawing into a passive image: nothing in it runs, animates or fetches, and its ids never meet the document's.
